# Ortaq 2.0 implementation plan

**Scope authority:** This file controls new V2 implementation. `PLAN.md` phases A–G are a completed historical record; do not edit their tasks or checkboxes. The stricter safety/security rule in any applicable instruction wins. Functional details are in [spec](docs/ORTAQ_V2_SPEC.md), schema and transaction rules in [architecture](docs/ORTAQ_V2_ARCHITECTURE.md), evidence in [test matrix](docs/ORTAQ_V2_TEST_MATRIX.md), and release steps in [release guide](docs/ORTAQ_V2_RELEASE.md). Work on `dev` only. A user-authorized batch may cover several dependency-ready tasks in ID order, with separate task commits and one full-suite run after the batch.

## How to execute and resume

1. Read this plan and the linked specification, architecture and test row. Check `git status --short --branch` and ensure `dev`; never overwrite unrelated changes or commit secrets, `.env`, `data/`, `target/`, database files or logs. Never run a live bot or two pollers with one token.
2. Pick the first unchecked task below whose dependencies are checked. In an authorized batch, continue to the next eligible task after each task commit; if blocked, record the precise blocker and continue only tasks with satisfied dependencies. Read only relevant code. Write the indicated regression/unit/integration test **before** a bug fix, observe its failure, then implement the smallest change. Use fake bot credentials and in-memory H2; human uses a separate dev bot for Telegram checks.
3. Run focused tests for each task and `./mvnw.cmd -q test` in PowerShell after the batch. Before each commit run `git diff --check` and inspect the scoped diff/status. Complete a manual check in a dev group if a human has done it; otherwise record `Manual: pending` in Progress and do not claim Telegram verification. Record any failing gate under Blockers with task ID, command, observed result and next action.
4. A task is **Done** only when its exact acceptance criteria and focused tests pass, migrations (if any) are reversible at the application level and tested on a copy, localization keys are present, no sensitive/generated files are staged, the checkbox is checked, and its specified commit exists. The full suite must pass before closing the batch; if it fails, fix the regression or reopen the affected task. A manual Telegram check may be recorded as pending for non-release tasks; phase V2-08 cannot finish until all manual checks are actually done. Commit only the scoped files with the task's message. Push completed work to `dev` when authorized and possible; never to `main`.
5. Resume prompt: `Read AGENTS.md and PLAN_V2.md; continue with the first unchecked task on dev, honoring dependencies and recorded blockers.`

## Task notation

Each task line specifies **scope/files**, **DB**, **test first**, **acceptance**, **manual check**, **commit**, and **dependencies**. `DB: none` means no schema change. `Manual: dev` means test with the separate development bot in a test group; if unavailable record pending. All tasks inherit the Definition of Done above. Exact visible wording and button layout are in the spec; a test may assert localization keys and behavior rather than duplicate all prose.

## Optional future backlog — not part of V2 completion

Receipt OCR, fridge stock tracking, Mini App, paid or local AI assistant, Russian language switch, CSV export, payment rails, bank/card storage, webhook and multi-instance operation. Revisit only after V2 release and separate product/security review. The sticker reference and pack can lag core feature release; if unavailable, record V2-07 as an explicit release exception with owner/date rather than silently marking tasks done.
